title: adopt swift-markdown-engine and make markdown the pad's truth
design:
User's call (2026-09-04): the pad should be live-styled — markdown turning into
style as you type — and if Craft takes markdown on the wire, markdown should be
the pad's truth. This bead is the architectural change that follows.

Package: nodes-app/swift-markdown-engine, Apache-2.0, macOS 14+, AppKit +
TextKit 2 behind a SwiftUI wrapper, zero external deps in the core product.
API is NativeTextViewWrapper(text: Binding<String>) — the document IS a
markdown string, which is what makes it fit. Its parser owns "marker/fence
hiding, caret reveal, and incremental restyling", i.e. Obsidian-style live
preview: the markers hide and come back when the caret lands on them.

## What changes

Markdown becomes the pad's truth. NoteDocument stops being the document and
becomes the SYNC-SIDE value only — parsed from markdown when a push needs a
block diff against Craft's block ids, and built back into markdown on pull.

Deleted, with their tests: NoteRendering (markers drawn as characters, the
shedding, the caret arithmetic), NoteEditor's redraw/restore machinery,
NoteBlock+Splitting, NoteDocument+Marks. Roughly 500-800 lines, and it is the
hardest, most trap-prone code in the feature — see the traps
'attributes-are-inherited-onto-typed-text' and
'indent-and-marker-are-shed-separately', both of which stop existing.

Kept: NoteDocument, NoteDocument+Markdown, NoteDocument+AttributedString, and
NoteStore (ccp-2zi.4) — the store just trades in a String now, or in
NoteDocument built from one.

Open, and to be settled before writing code:
- The format bar and block menu. With live markdown the marker IS the command,
  so the bar either goes away or becomes marker insertion. Discoverability and
  the a11y labels both argue for keeping something.
- Theming is NSColor-based (MarkdownEditorTheme) and headings are a fixed
  fontMultipliers ramp, against CLAUDE.md's lean toward semantic Dynamic Type.
  Resolve deliberately rather than by accident.
- Sizing in a ~148pt card. Couples to ccp-ydj.
- One editor per pad needs a stable documentId, per the package README.
- Package.resolved will list HighlighterSwift and SwiftMath even though the
  core product links neither — verify with a resolve before committing to it.

## Why it helps the Craft plan

ccp-2zi.8's hardest problem is preserving Craft blocks CCP has no concept of,
solved there by a store-side sidecar of CCP-owned ids. With markdown as truth,
an unrepresentable block round-trips as literal markdown text — "unregistered
syntax stays literal text" is the engine's own rule. The sidecar may shrink or
go.

## Risk

Pre-1.0 (0.12.0), created 2026-04-28, 57 open issues. Mitigating: 14
contributors, 12+ tags in four months, and it ships in Nodes on the App Store.
Pin an exact version. This would also be CCP's first REMOTE package dependency
— the repo's policy so far is vendoring plus the PsymailKit path dep — so the
dependency policy in CLAUDE.md/PATCHES.md needs a line about it.

Survey that led here: ccp-zaj. Independent of this: ccp-hw0 still needs fixing,
since the sync side keeps parsing markdown either way.

title: a to-do does not survive a markdown round-trip
description:
Foundation's AttributedString markdown parser has no GFM task-list support, confirmed by running it: `- [ ] todo` parses as unorderedList/listItem whose text is literally "[ ] todo". NoteDocument+Markdown emits `- [ ] ` correctly, so the write is fine and the read is not — a to-do comes back a bullet with brackets in the user's text, and it compounds on every sync round.

Blocks Craft pull (ccp-2zi.6), where markdown is the wire format both ways.

Fix is in NoteDocument(markdown:) or the AttributedString bridge: on a .bulleted block, read a leading "[ ] "/"[x] " off the text and make it .todo. ~20 lines, no dependency — swift-markdown (cmark-gfm) would buy the same one extension and cost a dependency.

Test: extend NoteDocumentRoundTripTests with todo blocks, both states, indented. The existing round-trip suite has no to-do case, which is why this was invisible.

title: block kind commands: make a heading, a list, a to-do
description:
NoteEditor renders every block kind correctly but nothing in the UI can reach them — only inline marks can be applied, so a user cannot actually make a list.

Two ways in, and they want each other: a command (shortcut or control) that changes the block the caret is in, and markdown-style autoformatting — typing '- ', '# ', '1. ', '[] ' at the start of a line becomes the block it names. Autoformatting is the one that will get used; the explicit command is what makes it discoverable and what a selection of several blocks needs.

Both are structural changes, so both go through the redraw path NoteEditor already has (NoteDocument.hasSameStructure). Indent and outdent (tab / shift-tab in a list) belong here too — NoteBlock carries an indent that nothing can currently change.

The format bar appears on selection today; a block command has to work with only a caret, so its placement is an open question rather than another button in that bar.
close_reason: Block kinds are reachable three ways: markdown-style autoformatting on the line being typed, a block-kind menu that works from a caret alone, and indent/outdent with cmd-[ and cmd-]. Indent is now drawn (counted spaces, like the markers) so it can be seen as well as set. Review found two real defects, both fixed: autoformatting scanned the whole note and could convert an unrelated paragraph and drag the caret to it (now scoped to the caret's block), and reading the indent and the glyph as one marker stranded a bullet in the user's text when a space in front of it went missing (now shed separately, so backspace in the indent outdents and backspace in the glyph demotes). 236 tests.

design:
Read from the real docs (connect.craft.do/api-docs and its space/ and documents/
sub-pages), 2026-09-04. Everything marked UNCONFIRMED needs a live connection
before code depends on it.

## 1. What the API actually is

Craft Connect is not one API. A *connection*, created by the user in Craft's
Imagine/Connections tab, has a scope, and the scope decides what exists:

  space scope       /documents GET POST DELETE, /documents/move, /folders GET
                    POST DELETE, /tasks, plus all the block endpoints
  daily-notes scope daily notes and tasks
  selected-docs     block endpoints only, inside documents the user picked by
                    hand. NO POST /documents.

DECISION: CCP requires a space-scoped connection. One document per pad means
creating documents, and only space scope can. Under selected-docs the user
would have to hand-make a Craft document per pad and reconnect — not a feature,
a chore.

Endpoints CCP needs:
  GET  /connection            space metadata, urlTemplates, and the server's
                              own UTC clock
  GET  /documents             ids and titles; ?fetchMetadata=true adds
                              createdAt and lastModifiedAt
  POST /documents             {documents:[…], destination: "unsorted" |
                              "templates" | folderId}. Creates them EMPTY —
                              content is a separate POST /blocks.
  GET  /blocks               ?id=&maxDepth=-1&fetchMetadata=true
  POST /blocks               {blocks:[…], position:{pageId,"start"|"end"} or
                              {siblingId,"before"|"after"}}
  PUT  /blocks               partial update; "only the fields provided will be
                              updated"
  DELETE /blocks             by id

THE FINDING THAT CHANGES THE EPIC: for text blocks, PUT/POST take **markdown**,
not a bespoke block JSON. NoteDocument already has a markdown bridge from
ccp-2zi.1, round-trip tested. The mapping is written.

SECOND FINDING: the epic's fear — "a naive debounce-append duplicates the note
every 3 seconds" — was aimed at an API with no update. PUT /blocks updates in
place by id, so a push is a diff (PUT changed, POST new, DELETE removed), not a
replace. No delete-then-repost, and no rewriting blocks nobody touched.

Undocumented, and to be treated as hostile: rate limits, request size limits,
error bodies. Any non-2xx is "store unreachable" with backoff, never anything
destructive.

TRAP for whoever picks this up: api.craft.co is a DIFFERENT COMPANY (Craft.co,
company data), and searches surface its `x-craft-api-key` header confidently.
It has nothing to do with craft.do. Do not let a search result point the auth
work there.

## 2. Auth (rewrites ccp-2zi.3)

The docs say only: "Create an API connection in the Imagine tab in Craft, and
paste your API URL here." No header is documented anywhere. So the API URL
appears to BE the credential — a per-connection secret path.

UNCONFIRMED and blocking: the actual scheme. ccp-2zi.3 cannot be written until
the user makes a real connection and we see the URL's shape.

What .3 becomes: not "a token plus a space/folder picker". It is a connection
URL, held in Keychain because the URL is the secret, plus a folder chosen from
GET /folders. Everything else in .3 stands.

## 3. Block mapping, both directions

Push is NoteDocument → markdown → text blocks. Pull is blocks' markdown →
NoteDocument. One conversion, already tested.

Craft has ~14 block types. CCP's model has an equivalent for text, code and
line (divider) and nothing at all for image, video, file, drawing, whiteboard,
table, collection, richUrl or page. A round trip that reads a document into a
NoteDocument and pushes it back would DELETE every one of them.

RULE: CCP never deletes or rewrites a block it did not create.

The store keeps a sidecar per pad — the Craft block ids CCP owns, in order —
and blocks not in it are neither shown in the pad nor touched by a push. The
sidecar is configuration, so UserDefaults holds it without breaking the
no-local-text rule; it is rebuilt from a fresh GET /blocks whenever it stops
lining up.

Why the sidecar and not ids on the model: NoteDocument has no block identity on
purpose — content is the whole value, which is what makes equality mean
"nothing to write". Pairing a block with a backend id is the backend's
bookkeeping. Keeping it in CraftNoteStore is what ccp-2zi.4's "if the protocol
mentions a block, it has leaked" is asking for.

The cost: a pad can be a partial view of its Craft document without saying so.
The widget has to show "3 blocks not shown here" — that lands in ccp-2zi.7.

## 4. Conflict: both sides changed

Detect: per pad, keep lastSyncedAt (the server's lastModifiedAt as of the last
successful sync) and a hash of what was pushed. On activate, GET with
fetchMetadata=true. Remote lastModifiedAt newer than lastSyncedAt AND local
edits not yet pushed = both changed.

Resolve: nothing loses. The local version is appended to the Craft document
under a "Conflicted copy — <date>" heading, then the remote is adopted. With no
local storage there is nowhere else to put a recoverable copy, and the store is
the honest place for it — the user finds it in Craft, where they already are.

Clocks: compare against the server's utc from GET /connection, never the Mac's.
A skewed machine must not win every conflict.

## 5. Timing

Push: 3s debounce from the last keystroke, PLUS a flush on deactivate() and on
app terminate. A debounce that only fires while the panel is open loses the
last three seconds of every session, which is exactly the text the user typed
before closing the panel.

Pull: on activate(). Nothing else — no polling. Idle cost with the panel shut
is a stated feature of this app.

A pull landing on a pad being edited: it doesn't. A pull arriving while the pad
has unpushed edits is the conflict case above, not a silent replace.

## 6. Failure and offline

The widget renders three states, and only one of them is editable:

  loading      the note has been asked for and has not arrived
  ready        editable
  unreachable  offline, unauthenticated, or the store said no

THE MOST IMPORTANT RULE IN THIS PLAN: the editor is disabled until the note has
actually loaded. With no local truth, an empty editor over a failed read is the
one thing that destroys a note — the pad looks blank, the user types, and the
debounce pushes it over the real one. No text, no typing.

Unauthenticated is a normal state with a "Connect Craft" affordance, not an
error. A missing permission never blocks the panel, and neither does this.

## 7. First run

Pads live in UserDefaults today, under keys shared with upstream Vorssaint's
floating pad (the ccp-2zi.1 hazard).

Migrate, once, on the first successful connection: each pad becomes a Craft
document. The UserDefaults text is LEFT IN PLACE, not deleted — upstream's
floating pad keeps working off it, and a migration that went wrong has not
eaten anything.

NEEDS THE USER'S CALL: after migration CCP stops writing those keys, so the
menu-bar pad and upstream's floating pad stop sharing a note. That is a real
behaviour change and it belongs in PATCHES.md either way.

## 8. What .5 and .6 become

ccp-2zi.5 (push): no longer "replace-body". Diff against the sidecar — PUT
changed blocks, POST new ones, DELETE the ones CCP created and the user
removed. Debounce plus deactivate/terminate flush.

ccp-2zi.6 (pull): GET on activate with fetchMetadata, adopt when clean,
conflict-append when not. Owns the sidecar rebuild.

New work this uncovered: confirm the auth scheme against a live connection
(blocks .3), and "N blocks not shown" in the widget (folds into .7).
close_reason: Plan written from the real docs and filed as the bead's design. Two findings reshaped the epic: only a space-scoped connection can create documents (so CCP requires one), and PUT /blocks updates in place taking markdown, so a push is a block diff rather than the delete-and-repost the epic feared — and the markdown bridge from ccp-2zi.1 is already the mapping. Settled: unknown Craft blocks are preserved and never touched via a store-side sidecar of CCP-owned ids; conflicts append a dated 'Conflicted copy' to the Craft document so nothing loses; the editor stays disabled until the note has actually loaded, since with no local truth an empty pad over a failed read is what destroys a note. .5 and .6 rewritten, ccp-jmk filed to confirm the auth scheme against a live connection (blocks .3). Two things still need the user: creating that connection, and whether the pad may stop sharing a note with upstream's floating pad after migration.

title: Craft push: debounced block diff, one document per pad
description:
Push the pad to its Craft document ~3s after the last keystroke, and again on deactivate() and app terminate — a debounce that only fires while the panel is open loses the last three seconds of every session.

Not a replace-body. PUT /blocks updates blocks in place by id and takes markdown for text blocks, so a push is a diff: PUT the changed blocks, POST the new ones, DELETE the ones CCP created and the user removed. Blocks CCP did not create are never touched.

The block ids live in CraftNoteStore's sidecar, not on NoteDocument — see the plan on ccp-2zi.8, which this bead is written from. The markdown conversion already exists (NoteDocument+Markdown, ccp-2zi.1).

title: NoteStore: platform-agnostic storage behind a one-line backend swap
description:
The scratchpad stops storing text in UserDefaults entirely. Craft becomes the store, reached through a platform-agnostic protocol so swapping to Obsidian or Notion is a one-line change at the composition root.

Decided by the user: no local truth. UserDefaults keeps only configuration (retention, selection, the pad-to-document mapping) — never the note text.

The protocol is the deliverable, not the Craft call. Shape it around what any note backend can honour — list notes, read one, write one, create, delete, a modified date — and keep every Craft noun (spaces, folders, block ids) inside CraftNoteStore. If the protocol mentions a block, it has leaked.

Async throwing, per CLAUDE.md. A store that is offline or unauthenticated is a normal state the widget renders, not an error that empties the pad — with no local truth, a failed read must never present as an empty note the user then types over.

Supersedes the earlier 'local truth, Craft as mirror' framing.

UserDefaults stays the local truth. Craft is a mirror behind a sink protocol so a dead network or expired token can never eat a note.

title: README links upstream's docs as CCP's — security reports misroute to Vorssaint
description: The README rewrite (e9cddfb) presents SUPPORT.md, SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and CHANGELOG.md as CCP's docs, but all four are still upstream's, untouched by the fork. SECURITY.md sends vulnerability reports to vorssaintapp/vorssaint-utils/security/advisories/new, so a CCP security report lands in the upstream maintainer's private advisories. SUPPORT.md points bug reports at upstream's issue tracker. CONTRIBUTING.md is titled 'Contributing to Vorssaint' and describes upstream's layout, yet README cites it twice as covering CCP's layout and conventions. CHANGELOG.md is entirely Vorssaint releases with no CCP entries.
design: Rewrite SECURITY.md and SUPPORT.md as CCP's (real consequence, and conflicts on upstream merge are rare and cheap). Do NOT overwrite CONTRIBUTING.md or CHANGELOG.md — they are upstream files that keep receiving upstream commits, and overwriting them makes 'merge upstream/main' expensive, which the fork strategy depends on staying cheap. Relabel those two in the README as upstream's instead.
acceptance_criteria: No README link presents an upstream-authored doc as CCP's own. CCP has its own SUPPORT.md and SECURITY.md routing to bubblesunyum/control-center-pro. Docs that stay upstream's are labelled as upstream's.
close_reason: Rewrote SECURITY.md and SUPPORT.md as CCP's own; security advisories now route to bubblesunyum/control-center-pro with an explicit split for vendored upstream sources. README no longer presents CONTRIBUTING.md/CHANGELOG.md as CCP's — labelled as vendored upstream rather than forked, to keep 'merge upstream/main' cheap. Reviewed by reviewer-taste and reviewer-correctness (both clean, all links and claims verified against the repo); scripts/verify.sh passed. Committed 3d28645.

title: evaluate a third-party markdown/block editor package against the hand-rolled NoteEditor
design:
Surveyed 2026-09-04, twice: a web-search pass, then a GitHub API sweep that
found what the first pass missed. Recommendation: keep the hand-rolled editor.

## The near misses — the two worth knowing about

- nodes-app/swift-markdown-engine (Apache-2.0, macOS 14+, 970 stars, 103
  forks, ships in Nodes on the App Store): AppKit + TextKit 2 bridged to
  SwiftUI. The mature option and the only one built for our exact platform.
  But it is a LIVE-STYLED MARKDOWN SOURCE editor — the document is markdown
  text styled in place — not a block model. Adopting it makes markdown the
  pad's truth and NoteDocument a parse of it. Worth a real look if the block
  model ever proves to be the thing costing us.
- jxe/quagmire (MIT, macOS 26 + iOS 26, SwiftUI): an actual block editor, and
  its BlockKind is close to a superset of NoteBlock.Kind — including
  .unsupported(payload:display:), which is the preserve-unknown-Craft-blocks
  problem ccp-2zi.8 solves by hand with a sidecar. Host owns serialization, so
  a markdown-backed host is anticipated. 193 commits, one author, 4 tags, has
  tests, 0 stars, pre-1.0. Fit is the real problem, not maturity: it is a
  page-sized editor — nav mode, drag gutter handles, @-mention popovers,
  turn-into grid, pinch-to-insert — for a full-window notes app, not a ~148pt
  glass card in a non-activating menu-bar panel.

## Everything else, and why not

- MarkupEditor (stevengharris, MIT, macOS 14+): ProseMirror in a WKWebView.
  HTML only, no markdown in/out, so the Craft bridge would be rewritten around
  HTML. A WKWebView cannot be styled by the CCP design system, will not honour
  the glass, and is a live web process in a widget whose idle cost is ~0% by
  design. contenteditable focus in a non-activating panel is a known sharp
  edge.
- swift-rich-html-editor (Infomaniak): same contenteditable shape, mail
  composer scope, no block model.
- RichEditorSwiftUI (canopas, Apache-2.0): a wrapper over RichTextKit —
  character formatting and fonts, no block kinds, no markdown, 42 commits.
- Proton (rajdeep, 1.4k stars): the README says "iOS and macOS Catalyst";
  Package.swift declares iOS 14 and visionOS only. No AppKit. Out.
- STTextView / SwiftDown / MDEditor / CodeEditorView: source-style editors —
  markdown as syntax-highlighted plain text. A different product from a pad.
- MarkdownUI, and its successor Textual (gonzalezreal): render only. Textual
  could one day replace ScratchpadMarkdownPreview; it does not edit.
- swift-markdown (Apple, Apache-2.0, cmark-gfm): parse/emit, no editor.
  Measured against Foundation's parser it buys exactly one thing here — GFM
  task lists — for a cmark-gfm dependency. See ccp-hw0; ~20 lines does the
  same.

## Nothing from the apps themselves

Craft ships only a JS extension SDK (craftdocs/craft-extension-api). Notion is
closed web. Obsidian is CodeMirror 6 in Electron. anyproto/anytype-swift is a
real native block editor but iOS-only, an app rather than a package, tied to Go
and protobuf middleware, and under the Any Source Available License — not
usable as a dependency. A GitHub search for "block editor language:swift"
returns hobby repos at 0 stars; the category is one package deep.

## What the survey says about our own code

Nothing in the ecosystem models blocks the way NoteDocument does, so an
adoption is a rewrite of the model, the Craft mapping and the design-system
contract — not a deletion of code. Every WYSIWYG option is a webview, which
the panel, the glass and the idle-CPU budget all argue against. The
hand-rolled cost is concentrated in NoteRendering's markers-as-characters —
the shedding and the caret arithmetic — which is real but bounded and covered
by NoteRenderingTests. Revisit if Apple ships a block-aware TextEditor, or if
quagmire finds other users and a 1.0.

title: no way back from an autoformat
description:
Typing '- ' on an empty line makes a bullet, and there is no way to say you meant the characters. cmd-Z restores the text, the editor re-reads it and autoformats it again — the undo is eaten.

Every editor solves this the same way: the backspace immediately after an autoformat undoes the format instead of deleting a character, and nothing else does. That needs one bit of state in NoteEditor — the block position an autoformat just fired at, cleared by the next edit anywhere else.

Not urgent: the trigger only fires when the marker is the block's whole text (NoteDocument.autoformatted), so it can never rewrite existing prose. The cost today is only that a literal '- ' on its own line is unsayable.

title: divider is unreachable from the block menu
description:
Every block kind the model has is reachable from NoteEditor's block menu except .divider, which NoteBlockCommand deliberately omits.

A divider is not a paragraph wearing a different kind — it holds no text, so turning the caret's block into one either strands the text that was there or draws a rule with words after it. It wants an *insert* command instead: put a divider block in after the current one, followed by an empty paragraph to land the caret in, so the note never ends on a rule you cannot type past.

Placement: probably the same block menu, in its own section, worded as an action ('Insert Divider') rather than a kind.

title: panel width math with variable lane widths
description: Layout.fitsAnotherLane already measures real lane widths rather than a count, but it assumes the lane being offered is the default 300. Once any widget can be widened, the refusal rule and the panel's own width need to hold up — including a resize that would push the leftmost lane off-screen, which fitsAnotherLane does not currently cover.

title: resize grips in edit mode, snapping to size steps
description:
Edit mode gains resize alongside drag. Snap targets are the size steps and the lane grid — no guide engine, no freeform x/y.

Coexists with the existing hold-to-edit and drag-reorder gestures in ControlPanel/PanelEditor; see the open follow-ups ccp-2rh and ccp-518 before adding a third gesture to that file.

title: two-axis widget size, lane width derived from its widest member
description:
WidgetSize gains a width axis. Layout.laneWidth stops being the answer for every lane: a lane is as wide as the widest widget in it, which is already true for .screen (432 vs 300) but expressed as a special case in Dimensions.swift. Generalize it.

Height already works — WidgetSize.height is a floor and ControlPanel draws minHeight + fixedSize, so cards grow to content today.

title: layout schema: lanes of placements, not bare ids
description:
PanelLayout.Lane goes from [WidgetID] to a placement carrying the id plus an optional user size override. Must decode the existing bare-id file — the layout is user data (see the never-edit-layout-file trap) and PanelLayout's non-destructive round-trip of unknown widget ids is load-bearing; keep it.

Intrinsic default size stays on WidgetDescriptor. Only the override lives here.

title: scratchpad sync status in the widget header
description: Synced / pending / failed, in the widget header. Silent failure on a notes widget reads as data loss. An icon-only indicator needs an accessibilityLabel and a value per CLAUDE.md.

title: [epic] flexible widget sizing with snap points
description:
Widgets stop being one fixed lane width. Size becomes a user-settable, two-axis property stored in the layout, with resize grips in edit mode that snap to the size steps and the lane grid.

Deliberately NOT a freeform x/y canvas. The panel is anchored top-right and does not scroll; fitsAnotherLane already refuses lanes that would hang off-screen. Lanes are what make edit-mode drag tractable and PanelLayout forward-compatible. The snap points are the size steps plus the lane grid — no guide engine.

Key move: intrinsic default size stays on the WidgetDescriptor; what the user resized it to belongs to the layout (CLAUDE.md model/view split).

title: notifications and full disk access catch up slower than the re-read behind refresh
description:
`activate()` re-reads on the next main-queue turn, which is enough for the
fields the engine writes through a plain `DispatchQueue.main.async`:
accessibility, screen recording, camera, microphone.

Notifications and Full Disk Access do not settle that fast. Notifications wait
on `UNUserNotificationCenter.getNotificationSettings`, a round trip to a system
daemon; Full Disk Access is probed on a utility queue by listing protected
directories. Both can take tens of milliseconds, so the first frame after the
panel opens can show a stale value for them.

Harmless today: only accessibility and audioCapture gate a widget, and the
subscription corrects both of these when they land. It becomes visible the
moment a widget declares one of them in `WidgetDescriptor.permissions` — so
whoever wires the first such widget should read this first.

Found by the correctness review on ccp-ec8.

title: dashboard readyKids counts only direct children, nested epics undercount
Permissions updates buffers while panel is shut, leaks observation until next grant
description:
`PermissionsAdapter.deactivate()` cancels the watch Task, but a task suspended
on `for await` over an AsyncStream is not woken by cancellation — the loop
only reaches its `Task.isCancelled` check when the next value arrives. So the
stream never terminates, `onTermination` never fires, and the Combine
subscription to `Permissions.shared` outlives the closed panel until some
permission changes and wakes the loop.

Idle CPU with the panel shut is a stated feature, and this is an observation
running against it. The buffering is the same fault seen from the other side:
AsyncStream defaults to unbounded, so yields pile up with nobody reading.

Fixing this needs deterministic teardown, which means whoever calls
deactivate() must hold the thing being torn down — the adapter, not the shim.
That makes this and ccp-bn9 one change.
close_reason: adapter owns the subscription and cancels it synchronously in deactivate(); a shut panel now observes nothing

title: shim owns Combine->AsyncStream bridging that belongs in the adapter ccp-8ld.1 follow-up
description:
`SystemPermissions.updates` builds an AsyncStream over `objectWillChange`,
which is a paradigm conversion, not a restatement of a type. The bridge rule
(Sources/VorssaintBridge/README.md) says a shim may restate but not decide,
and the taste review on ccp-8ld.1 flagged this as the one place the rule was
being stretched.

The shim should re-export upstream's publisher as-is — that *is* a
restatement, since Combine is the engine's native shape — and the adapter
should own the conversion and the lifecycle.

Landing with ccp-ec8: that bug needs the adapter to hold the subscription, so
the relocation is the fix rather than a tidy-up alongside it.
close_reason: shim re-exports upstream's publisher as changes:; the Combine->async conversion and its lifecycle moved to the adapter

title: a layout with the same widget id twice in one lane resolves to duplicate LaneSlot ids
notes: LaneSlot.id is the WidgetID, so a lane listing the same id twice yields two slots with equal ids and a SwiftUI ForEach over [LaneSlot] renders undefined. Raised by reviewer-correctness on ccp-lr7.2, which declined to file it on the grounds that no mutation logic exists yet — but the path does not need mutation: PanelLayout.load() will happily return {"lanes":[["stub","stub"]]} from a hand-edited or partially-mangled file, and lr7.6 will ForEach it. Recommendation: fold dedup (keep first occurrence) into PanelLayout.normalized(), which is already the invariant-maintainer that prunes empty lanes and floors at one lane — same place, same call sites, no new concept. NOT done in lr7.2 because normalized()'s contract was agreed with laurel as exactly those two invariants and widening it was not mine to decide unilaterally. Cheap; do it before lr7.6 renders anything.

title: decide the layout save policy for edit mode: debounce and off-main
notes: lr7.7 saves the layout after every drag mutation. JSONFileStore.save() is synchronous blocking I/O, so a naive save-per-mutation writes the file on the main thread mid-animation. Raised as an async-API finding by reviewer-taste on ccp-lr7.2 and declined there: the store is Sendable and actor-agnostic on purpose, so a caller can move it off-main, and making load() async would stop applicationDidFinishLaunching from having lanes ready when it builds the panel. The real decision is a save policy — debounce the writes and put them off-main — and it belongs with the mutation verbs, not the store.

title: bd makes its own git commits, and they bypass the commit-msg hook
description:
Running 'bd dolt remote add' produced commit 815bc9b 'bd: update sync.remote' — authored as the user, not requested, touching .beads/config.yaml (it stripped the trailing newline, nothing more).

Two problems:
1. bd commits to git on its own. This repo's profile is conservative about git actions, and CLAUDE.md says not to commit without authority. A tool that commits as a side effect of a config read/write breaks that expectation silently.
2. The message names no bead. scripts/hooks/commit-msg would reject 'bd: update sync.remote' — the regex needs a ccp- id — so bd is committing with the hook bypassed. That is the same drift ccp-jze was filed for, except the bypass is not a human typing --no-verify, it is a tool doing it invisibly.

Nothing was harmed here; the commit is a one-character whitespace change. The concern is the mechanism.
acceptance_criteria: Either bd's self-commits are disabled, or the hook and the docs acknowledge that bd is a sanctioned committer and its commits are exempt by design rather than by accident.
notes: Found while wiring the Dolt transport (ccp-0t2). Same class of issue as ccp-jze, which removed the --no-verify advertisement from the hook.

title: the engine bridge, and the Permissions adapter
description:
Every upstream type is internal, and VorssaintEngines is a separate module, so
nothing in the engine layer is reachable from CCPKit today. This bead
establishes the seam that unblocks the whole widget epic, and adapts the one
piece of shared infra v1 actually needs.

Sources/VorssaintBridge/ is compiled into the VorssaintEngines module
(sources: ["Vorssaint", "VorssaintBridge"]), so its files are module-mates of
upstream and can re-export internal types as public. It holds visibility shims
ONLY — no branch, no stored property, no decision. Anything that decides
belongs in a CCPKit adapter.

Originally scoped as "port seven files". Six of the seven turned out not to be
v1 work, and the survey is recorded on the bead rather than lost:

- BoundedProcessRunner needs no shim: its consumers (DiskSampler,
  PeripheralBatterySampler, NetworkProcessSupport, MaxCapacityProbe) are all
  inside the engines module. Transitive, invisible to CCP.
- Notifier has no v1 consumer — upstream UI/, WhatsApp, updates, cleaner, and
  MonitorAlertService, which is ccp-mlw.
- HotkeyManager + GlobalShortcut: v1's definition of done has no global
  hotkey. Deferred to its own bead.
- LaunchAtLogin: unblocked (L10n is in Core/, not on the exclude list) but not
  in the definition of done. Its own bead.
- Defaults: shim individual DefaultsKey entries on demand as adapted engines
  need them, rather than porting 1730 lines of upstream preference surface.
acceptance_criteria: Sources/VorssaintBridge/ compiles into VorssaintEngines and re-exports what CCPKit needs; CCPUI imports no upstream type. A permission can be queried through a CCPKit adapter and its denial rendered as the panel's inline degraded state, unit-tested against a fake permission source across granted/denied/undetermined.
close_reason: VorssaintBridge compiled into VorssaintEngines as module mates, re-exporting Permissions as public PermissionSnapshot/PermissionKind/PermissionAuthorization and SystemPermissions. CCPKit's PermissionSource/PermissionsAdapter sits on the seam, mapping WidgetPermission to PermissionKind, exposing PermissionState and unmet set for inline grant, with activate/deactivate lifecycle that refreshes and watches via MainActor-isolated task. Deferred yield fixes stale objectWillChange read, nonisolated watch fixes deinit isolation, Equatable added, Package manifest silences 34 unhandled-file warnings by excluding CCP siblings. Unit-tested against FakePermissionSource across granted/denied/undetermined/indeterminate, activate idempotence, grant while open, and deactivate stops watching. Follow-ups filed as ccp-bn9 (shim bridging belongs in adapter), ccp-ec8 (buffer while shut), ccp-5xe (nested epic miscount). ccp-78w and ccp-c2m split out as hotkey and launch-at-login.

title: revisit graphify integration - keep or remove
description:
Graphify was spiked on 2026-09-01 (code-only AST, 14,770 nodes / 40,672 edges, 5x token reduction on avg query, 2.3-17.8x per question). Installed as on-demand skill at .claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md (no always-on hook, no committed graphify-out/) to keep always-loaded cost at 4105 tokens.

Check in after ~2 weeks of real use:
- Are queries actually replacing 2+ file reads per lookup? Check opencode-stats-for-nerds / manual.
- Is the scoped corpus (CCPKit/CCPUI/ControlCenterPro) useful, or do we need to include selected Vorssaint dirs?
- Are duplicate-ID warnings or community noise bothering queries?
- Does the .graphifyignore need tuning?

Removal / turn-off instructions (complete, no step leaves a residue):
1. Remove the skill (the only harness-visible piece):
   rm -rf .claude/skills/graphify
2. Remove the graph + ignore:
   rm -rf graphify-out/ Sources/graphify-out/ .graphifyignore
   # also clear any per-subdir extracts if you ran them:
   rm -rf .claude/skills/graphify/graphify-out 2>/dev/null; true
3. Remove hooks if you ever added them (spike did not, but full install would have):
   graphify hook uninstall  # or: uvx --from graphifyy graphify hook uninstall
   git config --unset merge.graphify.driver 2>/dev/null; true
   rm -f .git/hooks/post-commit .git/hooks/post-checkout 2>/dev/null; true
   # verify: graphify hook status  /  bd memories check
4. Clean gitignore entry if you added one:
   Edit .gitignore and remove the 'graphify-out/' line in the CCP block (if present).
5. Remove the Python tool if installed isolated:
   uv tool uninstall graphifyy 2>/dev/null; pipx uninstall graphifyy 2>/dev/null; true
   # if you only used uvx --from graphifyy, nothing to uninstall.
6. Bless the harness (removing the skill changes tracked docs):
   scripts/context.py bless
   scripts/verify.sh --quick  # should still pass
7. Close this bead:
   bd close ccp-4q8 --reason 'kept|removed because ...'

multi-display placement: open on the display holding the status item
description:
Split out of ccp-lr7.4, which now covers dismissal only. The panel should appear on the display holding the status item (or, failing that, the one under the mouse), and anchor correctly there — including with the menu bar auto-hidden and with displays of differing scale factors.

Deprioritised deliberately: single-display placement is what the shell is being designed and reviewed against for now, and the multi-display case needs hardware to verify honestly rather than reasoning about NSScreen.
acceptance_criteria: With two displays attached, the panel opens top-right of the screen holding the status item and is anchored correctly there; verified on real hardware, not asserted from NSScreen arithmetic.
notes: Moved out of ccp-lr7 when that epic closed. Not abandoned and not blocked on any code: its own acceptance criteria refuse an NSScreen-arithmetic argument and demand a second physical display, which no session has had. Everything it touches is one method, ControlPanelController.show(from:), which already asks the status item for its screen and falls back to NSScreen.main — so this is a verification task with a small fix behind it, not a build.
